events.title: The deaths of Mary I and Cardinal Pole
events.shortBlurb: Within twelve hours the last Catholic queen of England and her Archbishop of Canterbury both died, and with them the Marian restoration…
body: Mary I, daughter of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon, had in 1554 reconciled England to Rome and, in 1556, installed the papal legate Cardinal Reginald Pole as Archbishop of Canterbury, the last Catholic to hold that see. Together they sought to undo the breach of the Reformation and to rebuild the old religion in the realm.

On 17 November 1558, about seven o'clock in the morning, Mary died at St James's Palace in London during an epidemic of influenza that ravaged the country. That same evening, about seven o'clock, Cardinal Pole — himself long ill at Lambeth Palace and only just informed of the queen's passing — died as well, nearly twelve hours after his sovereign.

The crown passed at once to Mary's half-sister Elizabeth, who would sever England from Rome again within a year. Pole lay in state at Lambeth and was buried on the north side of the Corona at Canterbury Cathedral. With the deaths of queen and cardinal on a single day, the Catholic restoration in England came to its end.
